questions.q: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to \left($0, $\infty\right) be strictly increasing function such that $\lim_{x \to $\infty}$\dfrac{f\left(7x\right)}{f\left(x\right)} =$1$. Then, the value of $\lim_{x \to $\infty} \left[\dfrac{f \left(5x\right)}{f  \left(x\right)} - 1\right]$ is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let, $x$ be any poistive real number.

$⇒ x < 5x < 7x$

$⇒ f \left(x\right) < f \left($5x\right) < $f\left($7x\right)$

$⇒ $\dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{f\left(x\right)}$< $\dfrac{f\left(5x\right)}{f\left(x\right)}$< $\dfrac{f\left(7x\right)}{f\left(x\right)}

$⇒ 1 < $\dfrac{f\left(5x\right)}{f\left(x\right)}$< $\dfrac{f\left(7x\right)}{f\left(x\right)}

$⇒ \lim_{x \to $\infty}1 < \lim_{x \to $\iinfty}\d$dfrac{f\left(5x\right)}{f\left(x\right)}< \lim_{x \to $\$iinfty}\d$dfrac{f\left(7x\right)}{f\left(x\right)}

It is given that, $\lim_{x \to $\iinfty}\d$dfrac{f\left(7x\right)}{f\left(x\right)} =1$

So, by using Sandwich theorem,

$⇒ \lim_{x \to $\$iinfty}\d$dfrac{f\left(5x\right)}{f\left(x\right)} =$1$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to $\iinfty}\left\${\dfrac{f\left(5x\right)}{f\left(x\right)} -1\right\} =$0$

$

$\lim_{x \to \dfrac{π}{4}}\dfrac{\cot^{3}x - tanx}{cos\left(x + \dfrac{π}{4}\right)}$

$= \lim_{x \to \dfrac{π}{4}} $\$left(\dfrac{1}{\tan^{3}x} -$tanx\right)$\$left(\dfrac{1}{2}$cosx - $\dfrac{1}{2}$sinx\right)\left[∵ cot\theta = $\dfrac{1}{tan\theta}\right]

$= \lim_{x \to $\dfrac{π}{4}} \left($1 - tan^{4}x\right)tan^{3}x . \left(\dfrac{1}{2}cosx - \dfrac{1}{2}sinx\right)$

$= \lim_{x \to \dfrac{π}}{4}}\dfrac{\left(1 - \tan^{2}x\right)\left(1 + \tan^{2}x\right)}{\tan^{3}x . \left(\dfrac{1}{2}cosx - \dfrac{1}{2}sinx\right)}

$= \lim_{x \to $\dfrac{π}}{4}}\dfrac{\s$sqrt{2}\left[\left($1 - tanx\$right)\left($1 + tanx\right)\sec^{2}x\right]}{tan^{3}x . \left(cosx - sinx\right)} \left[$∵ 1 + \tan^{2}x = \sec^{2}x \text{ and } a^{2} - b^{2} = \left($a - b\$right)\left($a + b\right)\right]$

$= \lim_{x \to $\dfrac{π}}{4}}\dfrac{\ssqrt{2}\left[\left($1 - $\dfrac{sinx}{cosx}\right)\left($1 + tanx\right)\sec^{2}x\right]}{\tan^{3}x . \left($cosx - sinx\right)}$

$= \lim_{x \to $\dfrac{π}}{4}}\dfrac{\ssqrt{2}\left($cosx - sinx\right) . \left($1 + tanx\right) . sec^{2}x}{cosx . tan^{3}x . \left($cosx - sinx\right)}$

$= \lim_{x \to $\dfrac{π}}{4}}\dfrac{\ssqrt{2}\left($1 + tanx\right)}{cosx . $\dfrac{\sin^{3}x}{\cos^{3}x} . \cos^{2}$x}$

$= \lim_{x \to $\dfrac{π}}{4}}\dfrac{\ssqrt{2}\left($1 + tanx\right)}{\sin^{3}x}$

$= $\dfrac{\sqrt{2}\left(1 + tan\dfrac{π}{4}\right)}{\sin^{3}\dfrac{π}{4}}

$= 8.

questions.q:
If $\alpha > \beta > 0$~are the roots of the equation $ax^{2} + bx + 1 = 0$, and
$\lim_{x \to \dfrac{1}{α}}\left(\dfrac{1 - cos\left(x^{2} + bx + a\right)}{2 ( 1 - \alphax{)}^{2}}\right)\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{k} \left(\dfrac{1}{β} - \dfrac{1}{α}\right), then $k$ is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Since,& $\alpha$~and~$\beta$~are the roots of the equation~$ax^{2} + bx + 1 = 0$, therefore~$\dfrac{1}{α}$~and~$\dfrac{1}{β}$~would be the roots of~$x^{2} + bx + a = 0$.

Let

$L = \lim_{x \to \dfrac{1}{α}}\left[\dfrac{1 - cos\left(x^{2} + bx + a\right)}{2\left(1 - \alphax\right)2}\right]\dfrac{1}{2} \to \dfrac{0}{0}$

$⇒ L = \lim_{x \to \dfrac{1}{α}}\left[\dfrac{2\sin^{2}\left(\dfrac{x^{2} + bx + a}{2}\right)}{2\left(1 - \alphax\right)2}\right]\dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ L = \lim_{x \to \dfrac{1}{α}}\left[\dfrac{\sin^{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\left(x - \dfrac{1}{α}\right)\left(x - \dfrac{1}{β}\right)\right)}{{α}^{2}\left(x - \dfrac{1}{α}\right)2}\right]\dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ L = \lim_{x \to \dfrac{1}{α}}\left[\dfrac{\left(x - \dfrac{1}{β}\right)2}{4{α}^{2}} \times \dfrac{\left\{sin\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\left(x - \dfrac{1}{α}\right)\left(x - \dfrac{1}{β}\right)\right)\right\}2}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)2\left(x - \dfrac{1}{α}\right)2\left(x - \dfrac{1}{β}\right)2}\right]\dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ L = \left(\dfrac{1}{α} - \dfrac{1}{β}\right)2\alpha$

On comparing this value with the value given in the question we get,~$k = 2\alpha$.

Hence this is the correct option.

questions.q: Let $a$ be the sum of all coefficients in the expansion of $( 1 – 2x + 2x^{2}{)}^{2023} ( 3 - 4x^{2} + 2x^{3}{)}^{2024}$ and $b = \lim_{x \to 0} \left(\dfrac{{∫}_{0}^{x}\dfrac{log \left($1 + t\right)}{t^{2024} + 1}dt}{x2}\right). If the equations $cx^{2} + dx + e = 0$ and $2bx^{2} + ax + 4 = 0$ have a common root, where $c, d, e \in R$, then $d: c: e$ equals
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: $a$ is the sum of all coefficients in \left(1 - 2x + 2x^{2}\right)2023\left(3 - 4x^{2} + 2x^{3}\right)2024$

$⇒ a = \left(1 - 2 \times 1 + 2 \times 1\right)2023 \left(3 - 4 \times1 + 2 \times1\right)2024$

$⇒ a = 1 . . . \left(i\right)$

Now, $b = \lim_{x \to $0}\dfrac{{∫}_{0}^{x}\dfrac{log\left(1 + t\right)}{t^{2024} + 1}dt}{x2}

Using L-Hospital's rule and Newton Leibnitz Theorem, we get

$⇒ b = \lim_{x \to 0}\d$dfrac{log\left(1 + x\right)}{\left(x^{2024} + 1\right)2x}$

$⇒ b = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{1}{2 \left(x^{2024} + 1\right)}

$⇒ b = $\dfrac{1}{2} . . . \left($ii\right)$

Also, $2bx^{2} + ax + 4 = 0$

$⇒ x^{2} + x + 4 = 0$, which gives complex conjugates as roots.

Let \alpha\text{and} \alphabe those roots.

Then, $cx^{2} + dx + e = 0$ will also have \alpha\text{and} \alphaas roots.

$⇒ d: c: e = 1: 1: 4

questions.q: If $\lim_{x \to 1}\dfrac{x^{2} - ax + b}{x - 1} = 5,$~then $a + b$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& $L = \lim_{x \to 1} ⁡ \dfrac{x^{2} - ax + b}{x - 1} = 5$

As~$x \to 1,$ the denominator becomes zero, hence~for finite limit, the numerator must also approach to zero as $x \to 1$

$⇒ 1 - a + b = 0$

$⇒ b = a - 1 \ldots ( 1 )$

Now $L = \lim_{x \to 1}\dfrac{x^{2} - ax + b}{x - 1} \left(\dfrac{0}{0}\right) form

By using L'Hospital Rule,

$⇒ L = \lim_{x \to 1}$\dfrac{2x - a}{1}

$⇒ L = \lim_{x \to 1}$\dfrac{2x - a}{1} =$5$

$⇒ 2 - a = 5 ⇒ a = - 3$

From the equation~\left($1\right),$~we get

$⇒ b = a - 1 = - 4$

$⇒ a + b = - 7 .$

$

questions.q: For each $t \in \mathbb{R},$ let  \left[t\right]$ be the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$. Then, $\lim_{x \to {1}^{+}}\dfrac{\left(1 - \left|x\right| + sin\left|1 - x\right|\right)sin\left(\left[1 - x\right]\dfrac{π}{2}\right)}{\left|1 - x\right|\left[1 - x\right]}$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\lim_{x \to {1}^{+}}\dfrac{\left(1 - \left|x\right| + sin\left|1 - x\right|\right)sin\left(\left[1 - x\right]\dfrac{π}{2}\right)}{\left|1 - x\right|\left[1 - x\right]}$

$= \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{\left(1 - \left|\left(1 + h\right)\right| + sin\left|1 - \left(1 + h\right)\right|\right)sin\left(\dfrac{π}{2}\left[1 - \left(1 + h\right)\right]\right)}{\left|1 - \left(1 + h\right)\right|\left[1 - \left(1 + h\right)\right]}$

$= \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{\left(1 - h - 1 + sin\left|\left(1 - h - 1\right)\right|\right)sin\left(\dfrac{π}{2}\left[1 - 1 - h\right]\right)}{\left|\left(1 - 1 - h\right)\right|\left[1 - 1 - h\right]}$

$= \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{\left(- h + sinh\right)sin\left(\dfrac{π}{2}\left[- h\right]\right)}{\left|- h\right|\left[- h\right]}$

$= \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{\left(- h + sinh\right)sin\left(- \dfrac{π}{2}\right)}{h\left(- 1\right)} = \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{\left(- h + sinh\right)\left(- 1\right)}{- h}$

$= 1 - 1 = 0$.

questions.q: If& $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\alphae^{x} + \betae^{- x} + \gammasinx}{x\sin^{2}x} = \dfrac{2}{3}$, where~$\alpha, \beta, \gamma \in R$, then which of the following is NOT correct?
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\alphae^{x} + \betae^{- x} + \gammasinx}{x\sin^{2}x} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\alphae^{x} + \betae^{- x} + \gammasinx}{x^{3}\dfrac{\sin^{2}x}{x2}} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\alphae^{x} + \betae^{- x} + \gammasinx}{x3} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Now using expansion of given function in terms of~$x$~we get,

$= \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\alpha\left(1 + x + \dfrac{x2}{2 !} + \dfrac{x3}{3 !} + \ldots\right) + \beta\left(1 - x + \dfrac{x2}{2 !} - \dfrac{x3}{3 !} + \ldots\right) + \gamma\left(x - \dfrac{x3}{3 !} + \ldots\right)}{x3}$

Now for limit to exist constant terms should be zero

$⇒ a + \beta = 0 . . . . \left(1\right)$

Also coefficient~of~$x$~should be zero

$⇒ \alpha - \beta + \gamma =0 . . . . . . . \left(2\right)$

Also coefficient~ of~$x^{2}$~should be zero

$⇒ \dfrac{α}{2} + \dfrac{β}{2} =0 . . . . . . . \left(3\right)$

So limit becomes,~$\lim_{x \to $0}\dfrac{x^{3}\left(\dfrac{α}{3 !} - \dfrac{β}{3 !} - \dfrac{γ}{3 !}\right) +x^{4}\$left(\dfrac{α}{3 !} - \dfrac{β}{3 !} - \dfrac{γ}{3 !}\right)}{x3} = $\dfrac{2}{3}

Now putting the value of limit we get,

\dfrac{α}{6} - \dfrac{β}{6} - \dfrac{γ}{6} = \dfrac{2}{3} . . . . . . . . \left(4\right)$

Now on solving equation~$1, 2, 3 \text{ and } 4$~we get,

$⇒ \alpha =1, \beta = -1, \gamma = -2$

Now putting these in all option we get,~$\alpha{β}^{2} + \beta{γ}^{2} + \gamma{α}^{2} +3 = 0$

questions.q: The value of& $\lim_{y \to 0}\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + y^{4}}} - \sqrt{2}}{y^{4}}$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
To solve this question, we need to apply the concept of rationalization twice.

Given limit is $\lim_{y \to 0}\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + y^{4}}} - \sqrt{2}}{y4} ( \dfrac{0}{0}form )$

$= \lim_{y \to 0}\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + y^{4}}} - \sqrt{2}}{y4} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + y^{4}}} + \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + y^{4}}} + \sqrt{2}}$

$= \lim_{y \to 0}\dfrac{\left(\sqrt{1 + y^{4}} - 1\right)}{y^{4}\left(\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + y^{4}}} + \sqrt{2}\right)} \times \dfrac{\left(\sqrt{1 + y^{4}} + 1\right)}{\left(\sqrt{1 + y^{4}} + 1\right)}$

$= \lim_{y \to 0}\dfrac{y^{4}}{y^{4}\left(\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + y^{4}}} + \sqrt{2}\right)\left(\sqrt{1 + y^{4}} + 1\right)}$

$= \lim_{y \to 0}\dfrac{1}{\left(\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + y^{4}}} + \sqrt{2}\right)\left(\sqrt{1 + y^{4}} + 1\right)}$

$= \dfrac{1}{4\sqrt{2}}$.

questions.q: $\lim_{x \to \dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(\dfrac{1}{{\left(x - \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}^{2}}{∫}_{{x}^{3}}^{{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}^{3}}cos\left(\dfrac{1}{{t}^{3}}\right)dt\right)$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let, $y = \lim_{x \to \dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{{∫}_{{x}^{3}}^{{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}^{3}}cos{t}^{\dfrac{1}{3}}dt}{{\left(x - \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}^{2}}$

$⇒ y = \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{{∫}_{{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - h\right)}^{3}}^{{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}^{3}}cos{t}^{\dfrac{1}{3}}dt}{{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - h - \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}^{2}}$

$⇒ y = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\dfrac{{∫}_{{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - h\right)}^{3}}^{{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}^{3}}cos{t}^{\dfrac{1}{3}}dt}{{h}^{2}}\right)$

Applying L-Hospital's rule and Newton Leibnitz Theorem we get,

$⇒ y = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\dfrac{0 + cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - h\right) \times 3 \times {\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - h\right)}^{2}}{2h}\right)$

$⇒ y = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\dfrac{sinh \times 3 \times {\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - h\right)}^{2}}{2h}\right)$

We know that, $\lim_{h \to 0}\left(\dfrac{sinh}{h}\right) = 1$

$⇒ y = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\dfrac{3 \times {\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - h\right)}^{2}}{2}\right)$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{3{\pi}^{2}}{8}$
questions.question: $\lim_{x \to \dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(\dfrac{1}{{\left(x - \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}^{2}}{∫}_{{x}^{3}}^{{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}^{3}}cos\left(\dfrac{1}{{t}^{3}}\right)dt\right)$ is equal to
questions.explanation:
Let, $y = \lim_{x \to \dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{{∫}_{{x}^{3}}^{{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}^{3}}cos{t}^{\dfrac{1}{3}}dt}{{\left(x - \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}^{2}}$

$⇒ y = \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{{∫}_{{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - h\right)}^{3}}^{{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}^{3}}cos{t}^{\dfrac{1}{3}}dt}{{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - h - \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}^{2}}$

$⇒ y = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\dfrac{{∫}_{{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - h\right)}^{3}}^{{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}^{3}}cos{t}^{\dfrac{1}{3}}dt}{{h}^{2}}\right)$

Applying L-Hospital's rule and Newton Leibnitz Theorem we get,

$⇒ y = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\dfrac{0 + cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - h\right) \times 3 \times {\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - h\right)}^{2}}{2h}\right)$

$⇒ y = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\dfrac{sinh \times 3 \times {\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - h\right)}^{2}}{2h}\right)$

We know that, $\lim_{h \to 0}\left(\dfrac{sinh}{h}\right) = 1$

$⇒ y = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\dfrac{3 \times {\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - h\right)}^{2}}{2}\right)$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{3{\pi}^{2}}{8}$

questions.q: Let $f: ( 0, \infty ) \to ( 0, \infty )$ be a differentiable function such that $f ( 1 ) = e$~and~$\lim_{t \to x}\dfrac{t^{2}f^{2} ( x ) - x^{2}f^{2} ( t )}{t - x} = 0 .$ If$f ( x ) = 1$, then $x$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\lim_{t \to x}\dfrac{t^{2}f^{2} ( x ) - x^{2}f^{2} ( t )}{t - x} = 0$
Using L'Hospital

$\lim_{t \to x}\dfrac{2tf^{2} ( x ) - x^{2}2f ( t ) f^{'} ( t )}{1} = 0$
$⇒ 2xf^{2} ( x ) - x^{2}2f ( x ) f^{'} ( x ) = 0$
$⇒ 2xf ( x ) [ f ( x ) - xf^{'} ( x ) ] = 0$
But~$f ( x ) \ne 0$

So, $xf^{'} ( x ) = f ( x )$
$⇒ x\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y$
$⇒ \dfrac{1}{y}dy = \dfrac{1}{x}dx$
Integration gives

$lny = lnx + lnc$
$⇒ y = cx ⇒ f ( x ) = cx$
Now

$f ( 1 ) = c = e$~(given)

So,~$f ( x ) = ex$
Now if~$f ( x ) = 1$, then $ex = 1 ⇒ x = \dfrac{1}{e}$

questions.q:
Let $x = 2$~be a root of the equation $x^{2} + px + q = 0$~and~$f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}\dfrac{1 - cos \left($x^{2} - 4px + q^{2} + 8q + 16\right)}{\left($x - 2p\right)4}, & x \ne 2p \\ 0, & x = 2p\end{cases}\right$.~Then $\lim_{x \to 2p^{+}} \left[f \left(x\right)\right]$
where \left[\cdot\right]$& denotes greatest integer function, is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$x = 2$~be the root of the given equation $x^{2} + px + q = 0$,

Putting~$x = 2$~in given equation we get,

$⇒ 4 + 2p + q = 0 ⇒ q + 4 = - 2p$

$∵ x^{2} - 4px + q^{2} + 8q + 16$

$= x^{2} - 4px + \left(q + 4\right)2$

$= x^{2} - 4px + 4p^{2} ( ∵ q + 4 = - 2p )$

$= ( x - 2p{)}^{2}$

Now, solving the~limit~$\lim_{x \to 2p^{+}}\left[f\left(x\right)\right] = \lim_{x \to 2p^{+}} \left[\dfrac{1 - cos \left(\left(x - 2p\right)2\right)}{\left(x - 2p\right)4}\right]

Let~$x - 2p = $\theta

$⇒ \lim_{\theta \to {0}^{+}} \left[$f\left($x\right)\right] = \lim_{\theta \to {0}^{+}} \left[\dfrac{1 - cos \left({θ}^{2}\right)}{ \left(\theta\right)$4}\right]$

$∵ \lim_{\theta \to$0}\left(\dfrac{1 - cos\left({θ}^{2}\right)}{\left(\theta\right)4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}~ ~(Using L'Hospital's)

$∴ \lim_{\theta \to {0}^{+}} \left[f \left($x\right)\right] = \lim_{\theta \to {0}^{+}}\left[\dfrac{1}{2}\right]

$∴ \lim_{\theta \to {0}^{+}}\left[$f\left($x\right)\right] = 0$

questions.solution: $\lim_{x \to \beta}\dfrac{e^{2\left(x^{2} + bx + c\right)} - 1 - 2\left(x^{2} + bx + c\right)}{\left(x - \beta\right)2}\lim_{x \to \beta}\dfrac{1\left(1 + \dfrac{2\left(x^{2} + bx + c\right)}{1 !} + \dfrac{{2}^{2} \left($x^{2} + bx + c\right)2}{2 !} + . . .\right) - 1 - $2\left($x^{2} + bx + c\right)}{ \left(x - \beta\right)2}\lim_{x \to $\b$beta}\dfrac{2  \left($x^{2} + bx + c\right)2}{ \left(x - \beta\right)2}\lim_{x \to $\bbeta}\dfrac{2 \left($x - $\alpha\right)$2  \left($x - $\beta\right)$2}{ \left(x - \beta\right)2}2  \left(\beta - \alpha\right)2 = $2 \left($b^{2} - 4c\right)$

questions.q: For $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \in \mathbf{R}$, if $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{x^2 \sin \alpha x+(\gamma-1) e^{x^2}}{\sin 2 x-\beta x}=3$, then $\beta+\gamma-\alpha$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \lim _{x \rightarrow 10} \frac{x^2(\alpha x)+(\gamma-1)\left(1+\frac{x^2}{1}\right)}{2 x-\frac{8 x^3}{6}-\beta x}=3 \\ & \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{(\gamma-1)+(\gamma-1) x^2+\alpha x^3}{(2-\beta) x-\frac{4}{3} x^3}=3 \\ & \gamma-1, \beta=2, \frac{-3 \alpha}{4}=+3 \Rightarrow \alpha=-4 \\ & \beta+\gamma-\alpha=7\end{aligned}$

questions.q: $\lim_{x \to 0}\left(\left(\dfrac{1 - \cos^{2} ( 3x )}{\cos^{3} ( 4x )}\right)\left(\dfrac{\sin^{3} ( 4x )}{{\left({\log}_{e}\left(2x + 1\right)\right)}^{5}}\right)\right)$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$\lim_{x \to 0}\left(\left(\dfrac{1 - \cos^{2} ( 3x )}{\cos^{3} ( 4x )}\right)\left(\dfrac{\sin^{3} ( 4x )}{{\left({\log}_{e}\left(2x + 1\right)\right)}^{5}}\right)\right)$

Now we now that,

$\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{sinx}{x} = 1, \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{1 - cosx}{{x}^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{2} \text{ and } \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{log\left(1 + x\right)}{x} = 1$

Now using the above formula we get,

$\lim_{x \to 0}\left(\left(\dfrac{1 - \cos^{2}3x}{\cos^{3}4x}\right)\left(\dfrac{\sin^{3}4x}{{\left({\log}_{e}\left(2x + 1\right)\right)}^{5}}\right)\right)$

$= \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\left(1 - cos3x\right)\left(1 + cos3x\right)9{x}^{2}}{\left(\cos^{3}4x\right)9{x}^{2}}\dfrac{{\left(sin4x\right)}^{3}{\left(64x\right)}^{3}{\left(2x\right)}^{5}}{\left(64{x}^{3}\right){\left({\log}_{e} ( 2x + 1 )\right)}^{5}{\left(2x\right)}^{5}}$

$= \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{1 - cos3x}{9{x}^{2}}\right)\left(1 + cos3x\right)}{\left(\cos^{3}4x\right)}\dfrac{{\left(\dfrac{sin4x}{4x}\right)}^{3}}{{\left(\dfrac{{\log}_{e} ( 2x + 1 )}{2x}\right)}^{5}} \times \dfrac{9 \times 64}{32}$

$= \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) \times \left(2\right)}{\left(1\right)}\dfrac{{\left(1\right)}^{3}}{{\left(1\right)}^{5}} \times \dfrac{9 \times 64}{32}$

$= \dfrac{9 \times 2}{1} = 18$

questions.q: If $\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty}\left(\left(\frac{\mathrm{e}}{1-\mathrm{e}}\right)\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}}-\frac{x}{1+x}\right)\right)^x=\alpha$, then the value of $\frac{\log _{\mathrm{e}} \alpha}{1+\log _{\mathrm{e}} \alpha}$ equals :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \alpha=\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty}\left(\left(\frac{\mathrm{e}}{1-\mathrm{e}}\right)\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}}-\frac{\mathrm{x}}{1+\mathrm{x}}\right)\right)^{\mathrm{x}}\left(1^{\infty} \text { form }\right) \\ & \therefore \alpha=\mathrme^{\mathrm{L}} \\ & \text { Where } \mathrm{L}=\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \mathrm{x}\left(\left(\frac{\mathrm{e}}{1-\mathrm{e}}\right)\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}}-\frac{\mathrm{x}}{1+\mathrm{x}}\right)-1\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{L}=\lim _{\mathrm{x} \rightarrow \infty}\left(\frac{\mathrm{e}}{1-\mathrm{e}}\right) \mathrm{x}\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}}-\frac{\mathrm{x}}{1+\mathrm{x}}-\left(\frac{1-\mathrm{e}}{\mathrm{e}}\right)\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{L}=\frac{\mathrm{e}}{1-\mathrm{e}} \lim _{\mathrm{x} \rightarrow \infty} \mathrm{x}\left(1-\frac{\mathrm{x}}{1+\mathrm{x}}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{L}=\frac{\mathrm{e}}{1-\mathrm{e}} \lim _{\mathrm{x} \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{x}+1} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{~L}=\frac{\mathrm{e}}{1-\mathrm{e}} \cdot 1 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{~L}=\frac{\mathrm{e}}{1-\mathrm{e}} \\ & \therefore \alpha=\mathrme^{\frac{\mathrm{e}}{1-\mathrm{e}}} \Rightarrow \log \alpha=\frac{\mathrm{e}}{1-\mathrm{e}} \\ & \therefore \text { Required value }=\frac{\frac{\mathrm{e}}{1-\mathrm{e}}}{1+\frac{\mathrm{e}}{1-\mathrm{e}}}=\mathrm{e}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $f$ be a differentiable function in the interval $(0, \infty)$ such that $f(1)=1$ and $\lim _{t \rightarrow x} \frac{t^2 f(x)-x^2 f(t)}{t-x}=1$ for each $x \gt 0$. Then $2 f(2)+3 f(3)$ is equal to _______
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \lim _{t \rightarrow x} \frac{t^2 f(x)-x^2 f(t)}{t-x}=1 \\
& \lim _{t \rightarrow x} \frac{2 t . f(x)-x^2 f^{\prime}(x)}{1}=1 \\
& 2 x \cdot f(x)-x 2 f^{\prime}(x)=1 \\
& \frac{d y}{d x}-\frac{2}{x} \cdot y=\frac{-1}{x^2} \\
& \text { I.f. }=e^{\int-\frac{2}{x} d x}=\frac{1}{x^2} \\
& \therefore \frac{y}{x^2}=\int-\frac{1}{x^4} d x+C \\
& \frac{y}{x^2}=\frac{1}{3 x^3}+C
\end{aligned}$
Put $f(1)=1\begin{aligned} & C=\frac{2}{3} \\ & y=\frac{1}{3 x}+\frac{2 x^2}{3} \\ & y=\frac{2 x^3+1}{3 x} \\ & f(2)=\frac{17}{6} \\ & f(3)=\frac{55}{9} \\ & 2 f(2)+3 f(3)=\frac{17}{3}+\frac{55}{3}=\frac{72}{3}=24\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If& $\lim_{x \to 1}\left(\dfrac{sin\left(3x^{2} - 4x + 1\right) - x^{2} + 1}{2x^{3} - 7x^{2} + ax + b}\right) = - 2$, then the value of~  \left(a - b\right)$& is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& $\lim_{x \to 1}\left(\dfrac{sin \left(3x^{2} - 4x + 1\right) - x^{2} + 1}{2x^{3} - 7x^{2} + ax + b}\right) = - 2 . . . \left(i\right)$

Putting~$x = 1$~in~limit we get

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 1}\left(\dfrac{sin0 - 1 + 1}{2 - 7 + a + b}\right) = -$2$~$⇒ \lim_{x \to 1}\$left(\dfrac{0}${a + b - 5}\right) = -$2$

For limit to exist~$a + b - 5$~should be zero

so $a + b - 5 = 0$~$⇒ a + b = 5 . . . \left(ii\right)$

Now Using L-Hospital in equation~ \left(i\right)$~we get

$\lim_{x \to $1}\dfrac{cos\left(3x^{2} - 4x + 1\right)\left(6x - 4\right) - 2x}{6x^{2} - 14x + a} = -2$

Again putting~$x = 1$~we get

$⇒ \lim_{x \to $1}\dfrac{\left($cos0\right) \times \left(6 - 4\right) - 2}{6 - 14 + a} = -2$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to $1}\dfrac{0}{a - 8} = -2$

Again for limit to exist~$a - 8 = 0 ⇒ a = 8$

So from equation~ \left($ii\right)$~we get

$8 + b = 5 ⇒ b = - 3$

So $a - b = 8 - \left(-$3\right) = 11$

$

questions.q: If $\operatorname{Lim}_{x \rightarrow 0}\left(\frac{\tan x}{x}\right)^{\frac{1}{x^2}}=p$, then $96 \log _e p$ is equal to ______
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$P=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}\left(\frac{\tan x}{x}\right)^{\frac{1}{x^2}}$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{P}=\mathrme^{\lim _{\mathrm{x} \rightarrow 0}\left(\frac{\tan x-\mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{x}^3}\right)}$
$=\mathrme^{\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\left(x+\frac{x^3}{3}+\frac{2 x^5}{15}+\ldots . .-x\right)}{x^3}}$
$=e^{1 / 3}$
$\therefore 96 \log _{\mathrm{e}}^{\mathrm{p}}=96 \times \frac{1}{3}=32$

questions.q: If $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{a{e}^{x} - bcosx + c{e}^{- x}}{xsinx} = 2$, then $a + b + c$ is equal to ________.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{a{e}^{x} - bcosx + c{e}^{- x}}{xsinx} = 2$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{a\left(1 + x + \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2 !} \ldots\right) - b\left(1 - \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2 !} + \ldots\right) + c\left(1 - x + \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2 !}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{xsinx}{x}\right)x} = 2$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{a\left(1 + x + \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2 !} \ldots\right) - b\left(1 - \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2 !} + \ldots\right) + c\left(1 - x + \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2 !}\right)}{{x}^{2}} = 2\left(∵ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{sinx}{x} = 1\right)$

For the given limit to exist numerator should be $0, \text{when}x \to 0 .$

Then, $a - b + c = 0$ $. . . ( i )$

Applying L'Hospital's rule, we get

$\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{a\left(1 + \dfrac{2x}{2 !} \ldots\right) - b\left(- \dfrac{2x}{2 !} + \ldots\right) + c\left(- 1 + \dfrac{2x}{2 !}\right)}{2x} = 2$

Again, for the given limit to exist numerator should be $0, \text{when}x \to 0 .$

Then, $a - c = 0 . . . \left(ii\right)$

Applying, L'Hospital's rule, we get

$\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{a\left(1 + \ldots\right) - b\left(- 1 + \ldots\right) + c\left(1\right)}{2} = 2$

$⇒ \dfrac{a + b + c}{2} = 2$

$⇒ a + b + c = 4$

questions.q: Let \left\{x\right\}$ denote the fractional part of $x$ and $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{\cos^{- 1}\left(1 - \left\{x\right\}2\right)\sin^{- 1}\left(1 - \left\{x\right\}\right)}{\left\{x\right\} - \left\{x\right\}3}, x \ne 0$. If $L\text{and}R$ respectively denotes the left hand limit and the right hand limit of $f  \left(x\right)$ at $x = 0$, then \dfrac{32}{\pi2}  \left(L^{2} + R^{2}\right)$ is equal to __________.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{\cos^{- 1}\left(1 - \left\{x\right\}2\right)\sin^{- 1}\left(1 - \left\{x\right\}\right)}{\left\{x\right\} - \left\{x\right\}3}$

$⇒ RHL = \lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}f\left(x\right) = \lim_{h \to 0}f\left(0 + h\right)$

$⇒ RHL = \lim_{h \to 0}f \left(h\right)$

$⇒ RHL = \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{\cos^{- 1}\left($1 - h^{2}\right)\sin^{- $1}\left($1 - h\$right)}{h\left($1 - h^{2}\right)}

$⇒ RHL = \lim_{h \to $0}\dfrac{\cos^{- 1} \left(1 - h^{2}\right)}{h}\$left(\dfrac{\sin^{- 1}1}{1}\right)

Let $\cos^{- 1}\left(1 - h^{2}\right) = \theta ⇒ cos\theta = 1 - h^{2}$

$⇒ RHL = $\dfrac{π}{2}\lim_{\theta \to 0}\dfrac{θ}{1 - cos\theta}

$⇒ RHL = $\dfrac{π}{2}\lim_{\theta \to 0}\dfrac{1}{\dfrac{1 - cos\theta}{\theta2}}

$⇒ RHL = $\dfrac{π}{2}\dfrac{1}{\dfrac{1}{2}}

$⇒ RHL = $\dfrac{π}{2}

$⇒ R = $\dfrac{π}{2}

Now finding left hand limit,

$⇒ LHL = \lim_{x \to {0}^{−}}f \left(x\right)$

$⇒ LHL = \lim_{h \to 0}f \left(-h\right)$

$⇒ LHL = \lim_{h \to $0}\dfrac{\cos^{- 1}\left(1 - \left$\{- h\right\}2\right)\sin^{- $1}\left($1 - \left$\{- h\right\}\$right)}{\left$\{- h\right\} - \left$\{- h\right\}3}

$⇒ LHL = \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{\cos^{- 1}\left($1 - \left(-$h + 1\right)2\right)\sin^{- $1}\left($1 - \left(-$h + 1\right)\$right)}{\left(-$h + 1\right) - \left(-$h + 1\right)3}

$⇒ LHL = \lim_{h \to $0}\dfrac{\cos^{- 1}\left(-h^{2} + 2h\right)\sin^{- $1}h}{\left($1 - h\$right)\left($1 - \left($1 - h\right)2\right)}

$⇒ LHL = \lim_{h \to 0} $\$left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right)\sin^{- 1}$h \left($1 - \left($1 - h\right)2\right)$

$⇒ LHL = $\dfrac{π}{2}\lim_{h \to 0} \left(\dfrac{\sin^{- 1}h}{- h^{2} + 2h}\right)$

$⇒ LHL = \dfrac{π}{2}\lim_{h \to 0} \left(\dfrac{\sin^{- 1}h}{h}\right) \left(\dfrac{1}{- h + 2}\right)$

$⇒ LHL = \dfrac{π}{4}$

$⇒ L = \dfrac{π}{4}$

$⇒ \dfrac{32}{\pi2} \left(L^{2} + R^{2}\right) = $\dfrac{32}{\pi2}\left(\dfrac{\pi2}{2} + \dfrac{\pi2}{16}\right)

$⇒ $\dfrac{32}{\pi2}\left($L^{2} + R^{2}\right) = 16 + 2$

$⇒ $\dfrac{32}{\pi2}\left($L^{2} + R^{2}\right) = 18$

$
